senses.sense_definition: To make a forceful, disapproving protest, objection, or complaint.

examples.text: The angry customer began to <w>remonstrate</w> with the manager about the poor service.
Several players ran over to <w>remonstrate</w> with the referee after the controversial red card.

senses.sense_definition: To say or state something as an objection or protest.

examples.text: "You cannot change the rules now," she <w>remonstrated</w> before walking out of the room.
He gently <w>remonstrated</w> that the budget was already stretched far beyond its limits.

senses.sense_definition: To formally present or lodge an official objection or grievance, especially to a governing body or ruler.

examples.text: The assembly chose to <w>remonstrate</w> to the crown regarding the newly imposed taxes.
Representatives arrived at the court intending to <w>remonstrate</w> against the monarch's latest decrees.

traits.comment: Used in historical or formal political contexts

senses.sense_definition: To point out, demonstrate, or make something plain and manifest.

examples.text: The scholar sought to <w>remonstrate</w> the truth of the ancient scripture to his listeners.
He attempted to <w>remonstrate</w> how the proposed strategy would inevitably lead to failure.

traits.comment: Rarely used in this sense today
